explicit_validation.explanation: Both LLM and human evaluations are conducted but they assess different sets of criteria (LLM: coherence/consistency/fluency/relevance; Human: understanding/attribution/salience/conciseness) and no direct quantitative comparison or validation between the two methods is reported

prompts.notes: Paper mentions 'detailed prompts' are shown in Appendix B but the exact prompt text is not visible in the provided text

guidelines.notes: Guidelines described in main text: coherence assesses ease of understanding, attribution gauges consistency, salience determines important information inclusion, conciseness evaluates brevity

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM evaluates using UniEval dimensions while human evaluation uses complementary but distinct dimensions focused on practical summary quality aspects
